scores.Biological Plausibility_reason: The central PTPRC exon-4 splicing explanation and the roles of PTBP1, hnRNP L, SFPQ, and activation-dependent GSK3 regulation are biologically defensible. The claim that GSK3 phosphorylation causes SFPQ degradation is inaccurate—the reported regulation primarily involves phosphorylation-dependent sequestration—and the T-cell mechanism is somewhat overgeneralized to all listed lineages.
scores.Grounded Mechanistic Synthesis_reason: The response effectively connects lymphocyte activation, PI3K–Akt/GSK3 regulation, the PTBP1–hnRNP L–SFPQ splicing machinery, PTPRC exon-4 usage, and resulting CD45RA versus CD45RO display. The extension of this regulatory chain to monocytes, B cells, and NK cells is less directly developed than its application to activated T cells. No synthesis ceiling was applied because the principal focus-feature–target mechanism is explicit, multistep, and substantially integrated.
